skill.name: brag-doc-from-git
skill.description: Build an evidence-based brag document or self-review draft from your merged pull requests and commits, leaving visible gaps where results are unknown. Use for review season, promotion cases or resume updates.
skill.summary: Draft evidence-based career accomplishments from Git history, with links and explicit gaps for missing outcomes.
skill.author: agentkitco

security_audit.summary: All six static findings are false positives involving Markdown formatting, read-only history queries, or ordinary prose. The GitHub search lacks repository filters and can return private repository metadata outside the named scope, despite an explicit prohibition. No evidence found of malicious exfiltration, destructive commands, or prompt injection.

remediation.issue: The GitHub search can retrieve pull request metadata from repositories the user did not authorize.
remediation.suggestion: Add explicit --repo owner/repository filters for user-approved repositories before executing the search; request repository names when none are supplied.

static_findings.snippet: For code not on GitHub, use `git log --author="<name or email>" --since="YYYY-MM-DD" --no-merges --p
- **Result**: only if a number, quote or outcome was provided. Otherwise write `[GAP: what changed f
Do not read private repositories the user did not name. Do not guess names, teams or numbers.
- **Scope signal** (if supported): led it, did it alone, worked across teams, was on call, reviewed

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 18 opens a Markdown code fence around a GitHub CLI query, not Ruby execution or shell command substitution. The repository-scope concern is recorded separately.
Line 20 closes the Markdown code fence; its backticks are document formatting. The enclosed command reads pull request metadata without executing repository content.
Line 22 uses inline Markdown backticks to display a read-only git log command. There is no instruction to evaluate the backticks as shell syntax.
Line 35 formats a missing-outcome placeholder with inline Markdown backticks. The placeholder is output text, not executable code.
Line 24 explicitly prohibits reading private repositories the user did not name. This is a privacy restriction, not a reconnaissance instruction.
Line 37 requests evidence-supported descriptions of contribution scope, including leadership and collaboration. It does not request system inspection or infrastructure discovery.

semantic_findings.title: GitHub Search Exceeds Named Repository Scope
semantic_findings.description: The command uses --author @me without repository filters, so it can retrieve titles, URLs, and repository names from unnamed private repositories. This conflicts with the instruction to avoid unnamed private repositories and risks including unauthorized metadata in the draft.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The documented command contains no repository filter, while line 24 explicitly restricts private repository access. Actual exposure depends on authenticated access and matching history.

content.value_statement: Performance reviews are difficult when accomplishments are scattered across commits, pull requests, and personal notes. This skill organizes that evidence into a Markdown draft and marks missing outcomes for follow-up.
actual_capabilities: Collect merged pull request metadata with GitHub CLI or author-filtered commit history with git log.
Combine repository evidence with user-provided notes about mentoring, incidents, reviews, and other work.
Group accomplishments by theme, preserve dates and links, and merge related follow-up items.
Draft contribution statements, supported results, evidence links, and evidence-backed scope signals.
Mark missing outcomes with visible gaps and finish with ranked gaps and three priority questions.
Offer to adapt the completed document into a self-review, promotion packet outline, or resume bullets.
limitations: GitHub collection requires an authenticated GitHub CLI; local history collection requires access to the relevant repositories.
The documented GitHub query lacks repository filters and limits results to 200 pull requests; enforce scope and check completeness.
History alone cannot establish business impact, individual credit, or work outside Git; user context is required.
The skill produces a draft, not a verified performance assessment or guaranteed promotion outcome.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Self-Review
use_cases.description: Organize six months of engineering work into themes with supporting links and questions about missing outcomes.

use_cases.title: Develop a Promotion Narrative
use_cases.description: Separate supported ownership and collaboration signals from missing evidence before preparing a promotion packet outline.

use_cases.title: Refresh Resume Accomplishments
use_cases.description: Turn shipped work and supplied results into concise resume candidates without inventing metrics or overstating team contributions.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Brag Document
prompt_templates.prompt: Build my brag document for the last six months using only [owner/repository]. Restrict GitHub searches to that repository and mark missing outcomes.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: create an initial draft from one repository.

prompt_templates.title: Use Local Git History
prompt_templates.prompt: Use local Git history in [repository] for [author] since [date]. Group accomplishments by theme and include these additional notes: [notes].
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: combine local commits with work outside Git.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare Promotion Evidence
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a promotion packet outline for [date range] using only [approved repositories]. Apply repository filters, separate individual contributions from team work, and rank evidence gaps.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: evaluate contribution scope across approved repositories.

prompt_templates.title: Create an Audience-Specific Draft
prompt_templates.prompt: Use [approved repositories], [date range], and [verified outcomes] to draft a brag document, then adapt it into [self-review or resume bullets]. Restrict all searches to approved repositories. Exclude confidential details, preserve evidence links, and end with the three highest-value questions.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: produce a tailored draft with explicit evidence and disclosure boundaries.

output_examples.input: Illustrative input: PR #42 added retry handling; no outcome measurements were supplied.
output: What I did: Added retry handling for failed requests.
Result: [GAP: What changed for users or the team?]
Evidence: PR #42, using the supplied link.
Question: Is there a verified change in request failures after release?

output_examples.input: Illustrative input: A team delivered onboarding automation; I implemented validation. Supplied measurements show setup time fell from 40 minutes to 25 minutes.
output: What I did: Implemented validation as part of the team onboarding automation project.
Result: The team project reduced setup time from 40 minutes to 25 minutes, according to supplied measurements.
Scope signal: Contributed validation work; did not claim sole ownership.
Evidence: The supplied project links and measurement notes.

best_practices: Name approved repositories and a time window; ensure every GitHub search includes repository filters before execution.
Provide verified outcomes and notes about work outside Git, including your specific contribution to team efforts.
Review every claim, link, and confidentiality boundary before sharing the draft.
anti_patterns: Running the unfiltered GitHub search across all accessible repositories without confirming scope.
Treating commit counts or pull request titles as proof of business impact or individual ownership.
Replacing visible evidence gaps with invented metrics, inflated leadership claims, or unauthorized confidential details.

faq.question: What does the skill produce?
faq.answer: It produces a Markdown brag document organized by theme, with supported contributions, results, evidence links, scope signals, and prioritized gaps.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub?
faq.answer: No. It also describes collecting local commit history with git log for repositories outside GitHub.

faq.question: Can it establish impact from commits alone?
faq.answer: No. Results require supplied numbers, quotes, or outcomes. Missing impact remains a visible gap.

faq.question: How are private repositories handled?
faq.answer: The instructions prohibit unnamed private repositories, but the example GitHub search lacks filters. Add approved repository filters before running it.

faq.question: Can it include mentoring or incident response?
faq.answer: Yes. Supply notes about work that Git history cannot show, including mentoring, incidents, reviews, talks, and design decisions.

faq.question: Can it help with promotion packets or resumes?
faq.answer: Yes. It offers to adapt the final document into a promotion packet outline, self-review, or resume bullets.
